properties.name: NOT ESTABLISHED (2026-10-05): why a member store on the work machine (bluesky-queueserver) has data and no graph.id.json. Its fresh graph.meta.json carries no information: any refused open writes it. Reflow2 deletes no identity file. The store's own RocksDB LOG files name every path spelling that opened it, with times, and settle the question on that machine
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), 2026-10-05, triaging art:vscode-call-field-log-2026-10-05. Entry [defect?] of 2026-10-01: "`bluesky-queueserver/.reflow2/graph.id.json` is missing; `graph.meta.json` was touched today at 13:02. Cause not investigated — needs root-cause before anything is written about why." The same day's [works] entry praised the refusal it produced. Reporter on 0.76.0.

WHAT IS MEASURED HERE (scratch stores, 0.76.0, 0.78.0 and main):
- No reflow2 code path deletes a store's identity file. The only sidecar deletion is the temp-dir snapshot cleanup.
- A refused open writes graph.meta.json, creating it if absent. So "touched today at 13:02" is fully explained by the reporter's own refused call that day. It does not date the loss.
- Two path spellings never write graph.id.json beside the real path: a symlink to the store (the id goes beside the link), and `--graph-path .` from inside the store (the id goes inside, as ..id.json). See fact:root-cause-a-stores-identity-file-is-placed-by-how-its-path-was-spelled-2026-10-05.
- The RocksDB LOG and LOG.old.<epoch-microseconds> files inside the store record, at every open, the directory as the opener spelled it ("SST files in <path> dir").

CANDIDATES, still open on that machine:
(1) the store was opened through another spelling (symlink, `.`, a renamed path);
(2) the graph directory was copied or moved without its siblings (for example built in a scratch dir and copied in);
(3) the file was removed outside reflow2 (git clean -X in an upstream repo with `.reflow2/` in .git/info/exclude, a sync tool, a hand rm).

WHAT TO MEASURE ON THE WORK MACHINE (read-only), from the bluesky-queueserver checkout:
1. `ls -la --time-style=full-iso .reflow2/ .reflow2/graph/`. Which siblings sit beside the store? Measured on 0.76.0: any `--call` or MCP session that opened it at this spelling writes graph.client.json and graph.usage.jsonl, and an `--import` writes graph.sync.json. Siblings dated before the loss mean the id file existed here and was removed (3). Only graph.meta.json, and nothing older, means no open ever succeeded at this spelling, so (1) or (2). Also look inside graph/ for `..id.json` (the `.` spelling).
2. `grep -h 'SST files in' .reflow2/graph/LOG*` and `ls .reflow2/graph/LOG.old.*`. These list every opening path spelling and when (the suffix is epoch microseconds). A path other than this checkout's .reflow2/graph means (1). A first open newer than the oldest .sst file means (2).
3. `find ~ -xdev -name '*.id.json' 2>/dev/null` and `find ~ -xdev -lname '*bluesky-queueserver*' 2>/dev/null`. Then compare any id file's graph_id with the hub pin's dependency_graph_id for this member, in the hub export.
4. `cat .git/info/exclude`, `git status --ignored --short .reflow2`, and shell history lines that touch .reflow2 (cp, mv, rsync, rm, git clean).

RECOVERY, measured in scratch: put an id file holding the store's real graph_id beside the store as graph.id.json, and the refused open succeeds with the data. To check it, open read-only (`reflow2 read loop_status`) and compare_designs against the member's export, if one exists.

NOT ESTABLISHED: the cause on the work machine. No measurement there was possible from here.
